newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end stable with investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end stable with investors sidelined.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed stable Tuesday as investors generally remained on the sidelines in the absence of economic news, brokers said.
They added Wednesady's trade was also expected to show stable prices and low volume.

However, activity might pick up later in the week, they said. The three-day visit to Peru starting Thursday of South Korea's Prime Minister Kim Young-sam would likely draw the attention of investors and create a positive image of the country, they added.
Tuesday the General Index closed unchanged at 1,435.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index nosed down 0.01 percent to 1,976.0 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
Volume was a moderate 31.6 million soles ($12.7 million) as foreign investors continued to be absent, believed to be still concentrating their funds in U.S. equity markets, brokers said.
Also, the delay in naming a new Presidency Minister after Jaime Yoshiyama resigned last Friday from the key post made investors cautious, they added.

While investors were not expecting the ministerial change to have a big impact on government policy, they wanted to wait and see to what extent the new appointment would signal a change of style, brokers said.
"Investors are cautious first because Yoshiyama resigned and then because there has been a delay over his replacement," said Augusto Larco of local brokerage Peruval.
The presidency minister is responsible for controlling a large part of the government's budget.
Among leading stocks, benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed unchanged at 5.73 soles, accounting for 39 percent of the day's volume.

Brewery Backus y Johnston rose 2.0 percent to 2.55 soles, accounting for 13 percent of total volume. Tin- miner Minsur was the third most heavily traded stock as it jumped 5.5 percent to 24.00 soles in 10 percent of the day's volume.
In a total of 1,995 trades, 58 stocks rose, 17 fell and 25 were stable.
